headline: Lean's checkers back a Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof, Garry Tonon submits Sam McNally for Polaris gold, and Ferrari fume after Hamilton and Leclerc collide in Vegas.

upcoming.what: Full 'Beaver' supermoon, the first of four in a row
F1 Qatar GP, 16:00 Irish time (qualifying Sat 18:00, not a sprint weekend)
Cygnus CRS-25 launch to the ISS on Falcon 9, 15:47 Irish time
Rayman Legends Retold (PC, PS5, Xbox, Switch 2)
UFC Riyadh: Adesanya vs Magomedov, plus Ian Machado Garry vs Amosov (main card ~18:00 Irish)
F1 Abu Dhabi GP season finale, 13:00 Irish time

items.headline: Report: China's spy agency helped firms get banned Nvidia chips
items.summary: The New York Times reports China's Ministry of State Security ran an effort to help Chinese companies obtain restricted AI chips, while the WSJ traced a smuggling route from Southeast Asia. It adds pressure to the China-sales probes already hanging over Nvidia.

items.headline: Amazon closing in on $7.5bn Decart deal
items.summary: Amazon is reportedly near a deal for Decart, maker of real-time generative video models and efficiency software that could help run AI workloads on Amazon's Trainium chips. The price has crept up from about $7bn when talks first surfaced in October.

items.headline: AI server makers seek price rises on signed contracts
items.summary: Suppliers are asking customers to pay more even on deals already agreed, as memory and component costs keep climbing. Another sign the AI hardware squeeze is hitting prices.

items.headline: Industrial: AI is shortening attack planning against control systems
items.summary: Security experts say AI tools are cutting the time needed to plan cyberattacks on industrial control systems. Separately, the chip supply chain warns new US export rules now reach consumer chips too.

items.headline: Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof passes formal checks
items.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, released as roughly 175,000 Lean files. Over the weekend the Lean kernel and independent checkers reportedly accepted it, though mathematicians note an unreadable proof explains little about why it's true.

items.headline: Cygnus CRS-25 still on for Sunday
items.summary: Northrop Grumman's Cygnus is targeting 15:47 Irish time on Sunday 29 Nov aboard a Falcon 9, carrying about 5 tonnes of science and supplies to the ISS. Otherwise a quiet weekend for spaceflight.

items.headline: Why atom-based quantum computers may fix errors more easily
items.summary: A look at why neutral-atom machines, with qubits held in laser traps, could have an edge on error correction over rival designs.

items.headline: Tonight in Cavan: poor, rain and a near-full Moon
items.summary: Overcast with rain likely all evening (90%+ after 18:00) and gusty south-easterlies; sunset is 16:22. Even with gaps, the almost-full supermoon near the Pleiades will wash out faint objects. Try Tuesday's full Moon instead, or check for breaks before dawn as rain clears from the northwest.

items.headline: Binding of Isaac update pulled AI-generated music
items.summary: A new update shipped with AI-generated tracks, which have been removed; Edmund McMillen says he's investigating how they got in.

items.headline: GTA 6 hits 60fps via an Xbox Series X glitch
items.summary: Players found a quirk that unlocks 60fps on Series X, with the catch that some animations run at double speed.

items.headline: Désilets gives an update on witch game 1666 Amsterdam
items.summary: The Assassin's Creed creator wants to do for witches what he did for assassins. Nothing new on the watchlist (Witcher 4, Cyberpunk 2, Witcher 3, Borderlands 4) this weekend.

items.headline: Tonon kimuras Sam McNally to win Polaris title
items.summary: On his first Polaris appearance in nine years, Garry Tonon submitted Sam McNally in round one at Polaris 40 in Southampton, avenging his ADCC 2022 loss, then called out Ryan Hall.

items.headline: Rest of Polaris 40: Andrey edges Ozbek
items.summary: Fabricio Andrey beat Christian Ozbek on a decision, Espen Mathiesen heel-hooked Sam Gibson and Phil Harris triangled Vaughan Lee. Next big event: IBJJF No-Gi Worlds, 10-12 Dec.

items.headline: Ian Machado Garry faces Amosov in Riyadh on 5 Dec
items.summary: No UFC card this weekend; next up is Adesanya vs Shara Magomedov in Riyadh, where Garry (No. 1 welterweight) meets Yaroslav Amosov. Prelims about 15:00 and main card about 18:00 Irish time.

items.headline: Qatar winners make their call-outs
items.summary: Kevin Vallejos wants Alexander Volkanovski next, while Joaquin Buckley is urging Navajo Stirling to chase Carlos Ulberg on the way to a title shot.

items.headline: UFC cuts Chikadze, Gomis and Silva de Andrade
items.summary: Giga Chikadze goes after four straight losses; William Gomis's release, at 5-2 in the UFC, is the surprise.

items.headline: Ferrari furious after Hamilton and Leclerc collide
items.summary: Fred Vasseur called the intra-team clash in Las Vegas unacceptable, and Leclerc said he was embarrassed for the team. Post-race, Hadjar was penalised for backing up Russell and Perez takes a grid drop for Qatar.

items.headline: Haas keeps Camara for the last two races
items.summary: Rafael Camara stays in the Haas for Qatar and Abu Dhabi, giving up his F2 title fight; he's already signed for 2027.

items.headline: 2030 V8 rules to cap engine customers at two teams
items.summary: More detail on F1's planned V8 return: each manufacturer would supply no more than two teams. Quiet on the GT and endurance front this weekend.
